s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial papules with angiofibroma-like histology
salient_findings: Skin-colored, dome-shaped firm papules over the chin, nose, and perinasal region
Papules increased in size and number since age 18
Dome-shaped lesion with plump fibroblasts and increased blood vessels on histology
key_facts: 28-year-old white man
Papules first noticed at age 18
Dozens of skin-colored dome-shaped papules on the face
No hypopigmented macules, periungual fibromas, or Shagreen plaques
History of right renal transplant at age 14
Biopsy of facial papule showed angiofibroma-like features
Electron microscopy showed crystalline inclusions within dermal fibroblast cytoplasm
Conical-shaped teeth on dental examination

shortlist.label: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
shortlist.why_kept: Angiofibroma-like histology and facial papules are characteristic of this condition

shortlist.label: Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple facial papules and history of renal transplant are consistent with this syndrome

shortlist.label: Fibrous Papule of the Face
shortlist.why_kept: Histologic analysis showing angiofibroma-like features supports this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Lipoid Proteinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Crystalline inclusions within dermal fibroblast cytoplasm and conical-shaped teeth are suggestive of this condition

shortlist.label: Multiple Hereditary Exostoses
shortlist.why_kept: Conical-shaped teeth and history of renal issues may be related to this rare genetic disorder

raw.rationale: The presence of angiofibroma-like facial papules, history of renal transplant suggesting possible renal angiomyolipoma, and the specific finding of crystalline inclusions within dermal fibroblast cytoplasm on electron microscopy are highly suggestive of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex, especially given the age of onset and the combination of skin and dental findings.

rejected.label: Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic lung cysts, renal cell carcinoma, or other specific findings associated with Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome

rejected.label: Fibrous Papule of the Face
rejected.why: While the biopsy shows angiofibroma-like features, the presence of systemic findings such as a history of renal transplant and conical-shaped teeth suggests a more complex syndrome than a solitary fibrous papule

rejected.label: Lipoid Proteinosis
rejected.why: The absence of characteristic findings such as hoarseness, skin lesions with a different morphology, and the specific electron microscopy findings not matching lipoid proteinosis

rejected.label: Multiple Hereditary Exostoses
rejected.why: The primary findings are related to skin and dental abnormalities without evidence of multiple exostoses or osteochondromas
